text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a spike in streaming sessions yesterday that hit org X's quota and pushed embeddings jobs to fallback model. We should treat streaming requests differently for burst windows. :thinking:

sam: Yikes. Do you have numbers? How much of the quota were they consuming vs embeddings?

maya: Rough numbers: streaming sessions ~120 concurrent, avg tokens/sec ~50, pushed token budget by ~60% in 10m. Embeddings were small requests but queue latency skyrocketed. I think per-endpoint token buckets + concurrency cap for streaming would help.

jon: Agreed. Streaming is long-lived and a different resource shape. Token-bucket alone doesn't catch concurrent connections that lock HW. Suggest: per-key per-endpoint token-buckets + per-key concurrent-streams limit + burst window (30s) with smoothing.

linda: Also need fail-open behaviour for enterprise SLA customers. Maybe two tiers: reserve N concurrent streams per-org, plus shared pool. For hosted API keep defaults conservative.

maya: Here's a strawman config we could add to the routing layer:
```
{"quotas": {"chat_streaming": {"rate_per_min": 20000, "burst_tokens": 5000, "max_concurrent": 20}, "embeddings": {"rate_per_min": 50000, "burst_tokens": 20000, "max_concurrent": 200}}}
```

sam: Love it. Implementation questions: where to enforce? edge LB or control plane? Edge would act fast but duplication of logic across hosts.

jon: Put enforcement in runtime gateway (gRPC layer) with central config push. Gateway can do per-connection counters and short-term memory for bursts, and control-plane for long-term quotas and billing.

linda: How do we show this in Console? Ops wants visible per-route concurrency and burst usage. Add charts: concurrent_streams, burst_remaining, queued_requests.

maya: Also need telemetry emitted as metrics: per_org_per_route.tokens_used, .burst_used, .concurrent_streams, .throttles. Tag with model and deployment variant.

sam: For rollouts: feature-flag rollout to 10% of traffic, and add synthetic load tests. Also fallback policy: when throttled, prefer to fallback to non-streaming chat endpoint or to lower-capacity model.

jon: Edge-case: embeddings rerank jobs often batch—if we enforce per-request limits that hurt batch throughput. For embeddings/rerank prefer token-rate over concurrent cap.

maya: Good point. So per-endpoint policy shape: chat_streaming -> concurrency + token windows. embeddings/rerank -> token-rate + batching-friendly bursts.

linda: Action items: (1) prototyping quota shape in staging (sam + jon) (2) Console metrics + UI mock (maya + product?) (3) add test harness simulating mixed workload (linda)

sam: I'll create an RFC PR with implementation plan and perf numbers. Assigning to sam/jon for runtime enforcement.

maya: Thx. @quota-bot can you schedule a daily alert for orgs hitting >70% of streaming burst for next 72h after rollout?

quota-bot: scheduled alert created: streaming-burst-70pct, cadence: 1h, window:72h :white_check_mark:

linda: One more: add docs for customers explaining streaming vs embeddings quotas and best practices (prefetching, smaller chunking, client-side backoff).

maya: yep. I'll draft a short doc and add to Console tooltips. :thumbsup:

sam: SG. moving to RFC. :rocket:
